abstract: Cellular processes range from local interactions among a few proteins to micrometer-scale assemblies whose coordinated components give rise to emergent properties. A prime example is the actin cytoskeleton in protrusive structures at the leading edge of migrating cells, termed lamellipodia. Significant progress has been made in understanding the functional contributions of distinct actin-filament populations and associated proteins within lamellipodia. Yet, a detailed quantitative appreciation of how actin filaments form a spatially connected and interdependent network has been impeded by limitations of existing methods. Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) can visualize such biological entities at molecular resolution in native cellular environments, but its limited field-of -view constrains quantitative analysis of extended assemblies. Hence, how lamellipodial actin architectures collectively support productive migration is not completely understood. Here, we present a 3D stitching montage cryo-ET workflow that advances both methodological and biological frontiers through its application to lamellipodia. We combine large-area montage-tilt series acquisition with independent tile reconstruction, denoising, and optical flow-based three-dimensional stitching to reconstruct large regions of the leading edge up to ~ 100 m2 at single-filament resolution. Bridging molecular resolution and cellular-scale context allows comprehensive filament tracing and quantification of actin filament networks, providing parameters for models of force generation in motile cells. Our data reveal that the network architecture in a seemingly uniform protrusive lamellipodium is markedly heterogeneous. By mapping Arp2/3 branch junction-based connectivity, using the molecular resolution of our data, we show how branch-junction distribution and network connectivity vary as a function of filament density and distance from the leading edge. We also identify the complex coexistence of short, branched and long, unbranched filament assemblies. We provide montage 3D volumes and filament vectorizations through an interactive, open web-based resource for browsing and interrogating the data. Our work thus provides a quantitative reference for lamellipodial actin architecture and a scalable approach for large-scale cryo-ET.
